key_insight: lPINN shifts most of PINN training offline by pretraining nonlinear basis functions, then solves new PDE instances online with only a linear layer over frozen, physics-compatible features.
engineering_relevance: This can greatly accelerate forward and inverse PDE solving while preserving physics constraints, making it attractive for repeated simulation, calibration, and sparse-data inference workflows.
method: Offline learn continuous neural basis functions from solution ensembles
Pretrain basis using derivatives or physics residuals to make them operator-compatible
Online freeze the basis and fit only the final linear layer with PDE, boundary, initial, and data terms
evidence_signal: Evaluated on advection-diffusion, Burgers, and nonlinear pendulum problems, lPINN reduced solution/parameter errors versus vanilla PINNs and cut online inference time by about 1 to over 3 orders of magnitude, especially with limited residual or measurement data.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality and coverage of offline training solutions, so poor basis learning may limit generalization to new parameter regimes or PDE settings.
paper_title: Linearized PINN with pretrained nonlinear layers
